summary: Frontend E2E verification of STRATEX HABITAT H-013 Wave 1 Batch 2A — governed publication path via the legacy /api/steward/publish wrapper. Logged in as homeowner via 'Homeowner' Quick Demo Access on /login (data-testid=demo-homeowner), navigated to /steward, and executed both the happy path and the negative-control gate test using the specified data-testids. Both scenarios PASS with no code changes.

steps_executed_in_order: steward-ack-switch (toggled ON, data-state went unchecked -> checked)

negative_gate_enforcement.result: PASS — button is disabled while steward-ack-switch is OFF, so preview/publish are unreachable and the governed readiness gate is honored in the browser.

critical_code_review_comments: HomeSteward.js is ~1102 lines — above the 700-line soft limit. Consider splitting each step (Ask, Confirm, DesignStudio prepop, ScenarioCompare, BuildReady, PackagePreview, Success) into sub-components plus a hook that owns the 8-step state machine and API calls. Would also make the governed publish handler testable in isolation.

handlePublish sends acknowledged_blockers derived from readinessData?.required_acknowledgment_ids first, then falls back to conditional_blocker_ids. The governed backend recomputes readiness server-side and here required_acknowledgment_ids came back empty while conditional_blocker_ids=['RDY-DECK-CONDITION'] — the fallback correctly picked up the deck condition and the request succeeded. Fine as-is, but worth a code comment noting the fallback is load-bearing for CONDITIONAL blockers.

The Build Ready acknowledgment UX copy still says 'diagnostic scoping request' whereas the governed contract treats it as an explicit CONDITIONAL blocker acknowledgment (RDY-DECK-CONDITION). Copy is technically accurate but could be tightened to match the governed language (e.g. 'I acknowledge the North Slope deck condition needs on-site verification before final scope').

steward-published-success step still references estimateData.scenarios.low/high in the summary card; if a user ever reaches step 8 without estimateData populated (e.g. after a hot reload) this would throw. Guard with optional chaining.

handlePublish toast on error uses detail?.error_code === 'PUBLICATION_BLOCKED' — good — but does not surface which blocker(s) blocked. Consider showing detail.blocking_item_ids in the toast for faster homeowner comprehension.

success_rate.backend: not-tested-this-iteration (backend already at 100% per test_h013_publication.py + test_h013_http_gates.py)
success_rate.frontend: 100% (2/2 scenarios: governed happy path + gate negative control)

context_for_next_testing_agent: H-013 Batch 2A governed publish path verified end-to-end in the browser. The legacy POST /api/steward/publish is a thin wrapper — response.workflow.origin === 'legacy_publish_wrapper' and audit.details.publication_path === 'governed_shared_service' both confirm the single-path guarantee. Frontend testids proven: steward-ask-btn, steward-explore-btn, steward-confirm-btn, steward-to-scenarios-btn, steward-to-buildready-btn, steward-ack-switch, steward-to-preview-btn (disabled until ack), steward-publish-btn, steward-published-success. If backend adds a new hard blocker in future, the current UI only exposes ONE ack switch — additional required_acknowledgment_ids beyond RDY-DECK-CONDITION would not be individually surfaced.
rca of the issue: N/A — no bugs. Verified: (a) request body carries acknowledged_blockers=['RDY-DECK-CONDITION'], (b) response is HTTP 200 with status='published', non-empty opportunity_id and workflow_id, (c) response workflow.origin='legacy_publish_wrapper' and audit.publication_path='governed_shared_service' prove the single governed path, (d) steward-to-preview-btn is disabled when the ack switch is OFF, proving the readiness gate is enforced at the UI before any publish request can be issued.
